statements.t: Looking ahead, Forge 1 is central to Velo3D’s next phase of growth and is expected to significantly expand our production capacity as it becomes fully operational, enabling us to pursue larger production programs and capture opportunities across aerospace, defense, space and energy.

It is expected to significantly expand the Company’s manufacturing production capacity as it is brought to full operation, and to support demand from aerospace and defense customers for the Company's metal additive manufacturing solutions.
The Company expects Forge 1 to serve as its primary production and manufacturing center.
Additional information will be included in the Company's Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026.

Management is reaffirming its full-year 2026 revenue and non-GAAP adjusted operating expense guidance, is revising its gross margin guidance and reducing its capital expenditure outlook, and is providing an expected timeline for achieving positive net cash from operations and an updated expected timeline for achieving positive EBITDA as follows:

Additional information on the Company’s results of operations for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 will be provided upon the filing of its Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q with the SEC.

Management uses “Non-GAAP Net Loss”, “Non-GAAP net loss per basic and diluted share”, “EBITDA”, “Adjusted EBITDA” and “Non-GAAP Adjusted Operating Expenses” to evaluate operating performance, prepare budgets and forecasts, and evaluate performance for compensation purposes.

statements.t: The facility is expected to support the expansion of the Company's Rapid Production Solutions capabilities and increase manufacturing capacity.
Our operating results for the foreseeable future will continue to depend on sales to a small group of customers.

We believe that continued investments in our products are important to our future growth and, as a result, we will invest in enhancing our portfolio of AM solutions through certain research and development projects based on customer demand.

In 2025, we implemented a number of supply chain and manufacturing improvements in response and intend to continue to focus on driving further operational improvements during 2026 to reduce operating costs.
As we scale our production, we expect to reduce this timeframe.

The gross profit and gross margin for our products are varied and are expected to continue to vary from period to period due to the mix of products and services sold through a 3D Printer sale transaction, a Recurring Payment transaction, RPS offerings, services contracts, new product introductions and efforts to optimize our operational costs.

There was minimal federal and state income tax expense (benefit) recorded during the periods presented due to projected losses, and we maintained a full valuation allowance on the deferred tax assets as of September 30, 2026 and 2025.
We will continue to evaluate the realizability of our deferred tax assets and the appropriateness of the valuation allowance on a quarterly basis.

As we continue to execute these strategies, we expect future revenue growth to be driven by demand for our Sapphire and Sapphire XC systems, as well as continued expansion of our RPS printed parts business.
We do not expect Recurring Payment revenue to be significant as we continue to shift our focus toward 3D Printer system sales and RPS printed parts revenue.
We expect Support Services revenue to increase over time as our installed base of systems grows.
We expect these operational initiatives to reduce manufacturing costs and improve gross margins over time.

We continue to focus on accelerating production cycle times, reducing material and manufacturing costs and improving efficiencies on the production floor, which we expect to support improvements in gross profit and gross margin over time.

We expect research and development expenses to increase as we execute our refreshed technology roadmap, including investments intended to support customer demand for RPS, scale parts production, improve system utilization and efficiency, and enhance and advance our portfolio of additive manufacturing solutions.

We expect selling and marketing expenses to increase as we continue to invest in sales and marketing activities and pursue opportunities in markets demonstrating demand for additive manufacturing solutions, including the defense and aerospace markets.
We expect general and administrative expenses to vary based on the level and timing of investments required to support our business and strategic initiatives.
We expect our interest expense will continue to decrease as a result of our lower outstanding debt balances.

Less than $0.1 million of a provision for (benefit from) federal and state income taxes was recorded for both the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025 due to projected losses, and we maintained a full valuation allowance on the deferred tax assets as of September 30, 2026 and December 31, 2025.
We will continue to review our conclusions about the appropriate amount of the valuation allowance on a quarterly basis.
We expect a benefit to be recorded in the period the valuation allowance reversal is recorded and a higher effective tax rate in periods following the valuation allowance reversal.

Less than $0.1 million of a provision for (benefit from) federal and state income taxes was recorded for both the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025 due to projected losses, and we maintained a full valuation allowance on the deferred tax assets as of September 30, 2026 and December 31, 2025.
As of September 30, 2026, we had approximately $38.3 million of non-cancellable purchase commitments for components and assemblies, which are expected to be fulfilled over the next twelve months.
These purchase commitments support anticipated production requirements and are expected to be funded through our available liquidity.

Management evaluated the Company's liquidity in accordance with ASC 205-40 and considered, among other factors, current cash balances, historical and projected operating cash flows, recurring working capital requirements, non-cancellable purchase commitments, scheduled debt obligations and other contractual obligations and expected cash requirements during the assessment period.
The forecast retains the Company's contractual obligations, including its lease commitments and scheduled debt payments.
We expect our capital expenditures to increase in 2026 compared to 2025 as we invest in printer capacity and related facilities for the RPS expansion project.

The availability and terms of any future financing will depend on market conditions and other factors, and there can be no assurance that additional financing will be available on terms acceptable to the Company, or at all.

Actual cash requirements may differ from our current expectations due to changes in market conditions, customer demand, the timing of customer collections and vendor payments, macroeconomic conditions and other factors, and we will continue to monitor our liquidity position and capital requirements.
If inventory is shipped, we will accrue a liability under accrued expenses.

The Company expects revenue for the third quarter of 2026 to be in the range of approximately $19.5 million to $20.5 million, representing year-over-year growth of approximately 43% to 51% compared with revenue of $13.6 million for the third quarter of 2025.
